description_en: The Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mandira is located at the centre of Sunaguthi, an ancient Newar settlement located about 5 kilometres south of Patan Darbar Square. The Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mandira constitutes the densest and oldest area of monuments in Sunaguthi. It was built during the Licchavi period and reconstructed in 1553 by Viṣṇu Siṃha. The complex consists ofphalcās, wells,jaḥrūhiti,caityasandsataḥs. Its main entrance can be accessed via a seven-bay colonnaded structure to the west known as Dyaḥ Sataḥ (SUN4050). Dyaḥ Sataḥ has two storeys and a small door that separates it into two bays, with one outside the temple complex and one inside. The upper floor (known asdyaḥchẽ)houses three wooden statues of Mahādeva, Gaṇeśa and Kumāra. These statues are brought down only once every year on the full moon day of Caitra to celebrate the Pekhaḥ Jātra (the Four Palanquin festival).The Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mandira is located at the centre of a courtyard that measures 30m x 30m. It is believed that it originally had two tiers (probably gilded, seeD. VajrācāryaVS 2056, 19), but that these collapsed several times during various earthquakes. It was reconstructed by Viṣṇu Siṃha in 1553 (probably in a pagoda style), collapsed during the 1934 earthquake, and was then rebuilt again, this time in a dome-shape. The original timber elements of the temple can be seen at the Dyaḥ Sataḥ, where they have been reused as lintel beams and joists. Two old corner struts measuring 3.1m in length are still on show inside the complex. The main entrance of the temple is located to the west and can be accessed via a small stone stair flanked by two stone lions. Two Licchavi inscriptions can be found on either side of these lions. A number of bell-stands have been placed on the square base of the temple, which measures 11.15m x 11.15m. The temple has a five-bay colonnaded structure based on a single slab stone threshold. The largest threshold can be found to the south and measures W x 688cm D x 48cm H x 50cm. Four stone slabs have been attached to each of the four thresholds. The main sanctum has four doors with stoneliṅgaand stands on a squarejalaharībase. The colonnaded outer circumambulatory path is covered with large pantiles, and the main sanctum has a brick dome as its roof. The dome is separated from the rest of the structure by tiles, layers of cornices and dentil designs. The pinnacle is made of copper but has been painted in a golden colour and has a layer ofāmalaka. A base ring ofāmalakahas been made out of bricks and placed at the base of the pinnacle.As one descends from the base plinth via the small stair to the south, one might spot a stone slab (108  x 108 cm). This has been placed on the floor as a symbol of Kīrtimukha Bhairava. A stone statue of Umāmaheśvara is attached to its northern side and is flanked by two smallliṅgasfrom the Licchavi period. A coral tree (pārijāta)stands to the south of theliṅgas, and is believed to provide flowers for Lord Śiva (who is also known as Bhṛṅgāreśvara). There are many historical objects inside the temple complex. Amongst these, the statue of Nandī (230cm L x 88cm W x 140cm H) on a platform and a stonetriśūla(308cm H) in front of the temple to the west are particularly notable. These two objects are probably the largest single-stone historical objects in the Kathmandu Valley. A small two-tier temple to Jagannātha has been built at the south-west of the temple complex and is based on a square base of 137cm x 137cm. A recent stone statue of Hanumān has been established to the west of the main temple.The well located at the north-east corner provides holy water for the deities, as well as for daily and occasional rituals. A statue of Jalaśayana Nārāyaṇa (lying Viṣṇu on water) has recently been installed in the far north-east corner. On the eastern boundary wall of the temple complex, one can find a small shrine dedicated to Sarasvatī and attached to a two-tier Gaṇeśa temple. The land (referred to as Dyaḥ Keba) next to the southern boundary wall was used for growing vegetables in the past. However, it is currently unused. Next to the street, the open land to the east (called Svā̃ Keba) provides flowers for the deities and to be used in rituals. A long rest house (known as Tāhā Phalcā) is located to the northern end of the complex and stands as a boundary marker for the complex. The Yaḥsigāḥ (SUN0050, the place where theyaḥsi‘pole’ is erected during Pekhaḥ Jātra) and Halipatāḥ Phalcā (SUN4012, located to the west of Dyaḥ Sataḥ) are peripheral monuments of the larger Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mandira complex.The termbhṛṅgārarefers to a golden water vessel found by King Vishnu Simgh of Patan in a well, and the name of the village (Sunaguthi, ‘lit. goldguṭhī’) is supposedly derived from this.Devamālā Vaṃśāvalī(2013, 94) mentions that King Ratna Malla established this village with 300 houses in 1513 and organised an annual procession on the full moon day of Caitra. During the Licchavi period, Sunaguthi was a separate administrative unit called Bhṛṅgāra Pāñcālī. However, according to an inscription dated MS 65, the king rewarded the residents of this village for their help in making the statue of Jalaśayana Nārāyaṇa at Buḍhānīlakaṇṭha by granting them a level of autonomy regarding the administration of the area.The liṅgain the sanctum is one of the 64liṅgasof Nepal. It is believed that one can purify themselves by taking a bath in the Siddharasakuṇḍa located nearby the temple. In doing so, he or she enters the world of Lord Śiva. Although the date of its initial construction has not been traced out, theGopālarājavaṃśāvalī(fol. 17r), suggests that the Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mandira is older than the Paśupatinātha Temple in Kathmandu.
description_ne: 'भृङ्गार' शब्दको अर्थ सुनको कलश वा सुनको घडा हुन्छ । 'भृङ्गार' शब्दको अर्थ लिएर नै अहिलेको सुनागुथि / सुनाकोठी नाउँ रहन गएको हुन सक्छ । राजा रत्न मल्लले नेसं ६३३ मा भृङ्गारेश्वर महादेवको आज्ञाबमोजिम नै ३०० घरको सुनागुथि शहर बसाएर चैत्र शुक्ल पूर्णिमाको जात्रा संचालन गरिएका थिए (Yogī2013, 94) । सुनागुथिको मध्यभागमा रहेको भृङ्गारेश्वरको मन्दिर अहिले गुम्बज शैलीमा बनेको छ । भृङ्गारेश्वरको शिवलिङ्ग मानवनिर्मित नभएर आफै उत्पन्न भएको स्ययम्भू शिवलिङ्ग हो । चारपाटे जलहरिमा कमलपत्र बनाई त्यसमाथि शिवलिङ्ग स्थापना गरिएको छ । भृङ्गारेश्वर महादेवको शिवलिङ्ग पशुपतिनाथको जस्तो चतुर्मुख छैन । यो शिवलिङ्गको माथिल्लो भागको पूर्व-पश्चिम दिशाको केही भाग टुक्रिएर गएको छ । मन्दिरको अगाडि कलात्मक भव्य नन्दी, नेसं ७३४ मा चढाइएको त्रिशूल स्थापना गरिएको छ । मन्दिरको उत्तरमा पेटीसँगै जोडिएर जलकुण्ड बनाइएको छ ।मन्दिर प्राङ्गणमा रहेको द्यः सतःको उत्तरमा विसं २०६७ सालमा निर्मित जगन्नाथ, रामेश्वर, केदारनाथ, बद्रीनाथका प्रतिमाहरू लहरै राखिएका छन् । मन्दिरको उत्तर-पूर्वमा ज्ञानवापीकुण्ड भनिने इनार रहेको छ । भृङ्गारेश्वर महादेवको नित्यपूजा गर्दा यसै इनारबाट पानी लग्नुपर्ने प्रावधान रहेको छ । मन्दिरको उत्तर-पूर्वमा विसं २०६९ मा बनाइएको जलशयन नारायणको मूर्ति रहेको छ । त्यस्तै मन्दिरको दक्षिणमा उमामहेश्वर, कीर्तिमुख भैरव, पारिजात रूख देख्न सकिन्छ । मन्दिरको दक्षिण-पश्चिममा जगन्नाथ मन्दिर र हनुमानको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ ।लिच्छविकालमा यो ठाउँ भृङ्गार ग्रामको रूपमा विकास भएको थियो । लिच्छवि राजाहरूले यस ठाउँका बासिन्दालाई विशेष सुविधा प्रदान गरेका थिए । पछि मानिसहरूले यस मन्दिरबारे बिर्से । नेसं ६७४ मा ललितपुरका महापात्र शासक विष्णुसिंहले यस मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण गरिदिएका थिए । विसं १९९० सालभन्दा अगाडि यो मन्दिर तल्ले शैलीमा निर्मित थियो । विसं १९९० सालको भूकम्पले यो मन्दिर पूरै भत्किएको थियो । नेपाल सरकारले मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण गर्दा पहिलेको तल्ले शैलीलाई कायम नराखी हालको गुम्बज शैलीमा बनाइदिएको थियो । पहिलेको तल्ले शैलीको मन्दिरका केही अवशेषहरू अहिले पनि देख्न पाइन्छ । टुँडालको दुईवटा कुँसल (corner strut) लाई मन्दिरको उत्तरमा रहेको सत्तलमा सुरक्षितपूर्वक प्रदर्शन गरिएको छ । मन्दिरका केही काठलाई द्यः सतः(SUN4050)को दलिनमा पनि प्रयोग गरिएको देख्न सकिन्छ । धनवज्र वज्राचार्य (2056, 19) ले मन्दिरको छाना सुनको मोलम्बा गरी बनाइएको अनुमान गरेका छन् ।यो मन्दिरमा रहेको शिवलिङ्ग नेपालका ६४ शिवलिङ्गमध्ये एउटामा पर्दछ । भृङ्गारेश्वरको नजीकै रहेको सिद्धरसकुण्डमा चैत्र शुक्ल त्रयोदशी, फागुण कृष्ण चतुर्थी र वैशाख शुक्ल पूर्णिमाको दिनमा स्नान गरेमा जिन्दगीभर गरेको पापकर्मबाट मुक्ति पाई शिवलोकमा वास पाइन्छ भन्ने मान्यता रहेको छ (H. Jośī 2058, 397) । यो मन्दिर कहिले निर्माण गरियो भन्ने कुनै प्रमाण छैन । गोपालराजवंशावली (हेर्नू, Vajrācārya 1985, 25) मा पशुपतिनाथको प्रादुर्भाव हुनुभन्दा अघि नै भृङ्गारेश्वरको प्रादुर्भाव भइसकेको चर्चा गरिएको छ ।यहाँ पश्चिम नेपालको भट्ट ब्राम्हणबाट नित्यपूजा लगायतका पूजाहरू संचालन भइरहेका छन् । ती पूजाहरू संचालन गर्न गुठी संस्थानले पनि केही सहयोग गरिरहेको छ । भृङ्गारेश्वर महादेवको महिमा बुझेर नेपाल सरकारले भृङ्गारेश्वर मन्दिरको चित्र राखेर सन् २०१६ मा रु. २ को हुलाक टिकट प्रकाशन गरेको छ ।

historical_events.event_description: The statue of Jalaśayana Nārāyaṇa (a replica of the one in Buḍhānīlakaṇṭha) was consecrated in 2012 by the local residents.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of a statue of Hanumān
historical_events.event_description: Local residents collected donations and established this Hanumān statue in 2015.
This inscription of Bhīmārjunadeva and Jiṣṇugupta (r. 631-633 CE) is not directly related to this temple. It mentions that modern Sunaguthi was called Bhṛṅgāra Pāñcālī during the Licchavi period.

historical_events.event_name: Management of ponds and water channels
historical_events.event_description: This inscription of King Śivadeva (694-705 CE) mentions the management of ponds and water channels in Bhṛṅgāreśvara.

The inscription mentions that the temple was destroyed. It was reconstructed by Viṣṇu Siṃha in NS 674. It further informs the readers that his attendants excavated two copper vessels inscribed with the name of the deity Bhṛṅgāreśvara.
A Brahmin named Śrīnārāyaṇa offered a trident to Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mahādeva.

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of a Gaṇeśa and Kumāra statue
historical_events.event_description: A Brahmin named Mahādeva established a statue of Gaṇeśa and Kumāra near Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mandira. This event is also mentioned in the inscription from NS 734.
A Brahmin named Kṛṣṇadeva offered a golden parasol to Bhṛṅgāreśvara.
The temple was reconstructed in a dome shape by the goverment after it collapsed during the 1934 earthquake.

objects.object_name: A small shrine with various deities
